Know Your Mind

A MOMENT FOR YOUR MIND

How the check-in works.

36 questions. Six areas of everyday life. A clearer view of the responses you chose.

1. Reflect at your own pace

For each statement, choose how often it describes you: Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Often or Almost Always. There are no right answers. Answer all 36 questions to generate your report. You can save a draft in this browser and return later.

A check-in usually takes around 8–12 minutes, but there is no timer. Pick the answer that fits your recent experience instead of the answer you wish were true.

2. Explore six areas

Self-awareness

Notice feelings, reactions, assumptions and the experiences behind them.

Thinking patterns

Reflect on recurring thoughts, different perspectives and changing an approach.

Emotional regulation

Look at how you respond to feelings and return to everyday tasks.

Decision-making

Consider choices, uncertainty, consequences and what matters to you.

Relationships

Explore listening, expressing needs, understanding differences and boundaries.

Resilience

Reflect on adapting to change, finding help and caring for yourself.

3. Read your own response patterns

Your report shows the answers you selected, grouped by area, with reflections and practical prompts. Helpful habits and difficulties are worded differently: choosing a higher frequency does not always mean something positive.

This questionnaire is a self-reflection tool. It does not produce a clinically validated diagnosis, a mental-health percentage or a rank against the world. Any mock population examples inside a report are clearly labelled as fictional.

View a sample report with fictional answers →

4. Keep the reports you choose

Completed check-ins can stay in the browser where you took them. Anyone using that browser may be able to open its saved reports, so use a private device. Signing in does not automatically upload old browser reports.

When signed in with Google or email, your progress saves automatically so you can resume an unfinished check-in. Completing a test saves a separate dated report to your account. Starting a new test leaves your completed reports in place. Account reports are available on another device after you sign in to the same account.

You can delete individual account reports in My reports. Separate browser copies and downloaded PDFs remain until you remove them. See our privacy policy for details.

5. Compare check-ins over time

In My reports, choose a question and compare its recorded response across check-in dates. Select two reports to see what changed in all 36 answers. Comparisons use the same questionnaire and question language; they do not combine different tests into one score.

Only actual saved responses appear as points. Days without a check-in have no recorded measurement. Changes can give you a topic to reflect on, but they do not prove improvement, deterioration or an effect of treatment.

What this tool can and cannot tell you

Know Your Mind can help you notice and describe your experiences. It cannot diagnose a condition or replace care from a qualified professional. If you are concerned about how you are feeling, consider discussing it with a professional you trust.

Questions are available in multiple languages. Report explanations currently support English and Hindi; the language selector explains the available coverage. The FAQ covers common questions about using and saving reports.
